walkthroughs.body_html:
Direct taxes come straight off income — like income tax and National Insurance.

Indirect taxes are added to prices — VAT, fuel duty, tobacco duty.

Big UK taxes include:

  • Income tax — on wages.
  • VAT — usually 20%.
  • Council tax — paid by households to councils.
  • Corporation tax — on company profits.

Excise duty is extra tax on petrol, alcohol and tobacco.

Two jobs:

  • Raise money.
  • Put people off using harmful things.

That's why cigarettes are so pricey. 🚬

mcqs.q: What does standard theory predict about a minimum wage?
options: A minimum wage always reduces unemployment because workers have more money to spend.
If above equilibrium, it raises wages for those still employed but causes unemployment by reducing labour demand — though empirical evidence is mixed.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
A minimum wage is paid by the government.

mcqs.q: What are the functions of money?
options: Money is valuable because it is made of valuable materials.
Medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment — money must perform these to function as money.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.

mcqs.q: What components make up aggregate demand?
options: AD = C + I + G + (X - M): consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. A shift in any component shifts the AD curve.
Aggregate demand is just the total amount consumers want to buy.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
